title: Ohm's law: current, voltage and resistance
goal: Explore how the current changes with the voltage and the resistance.
note: In an ohmic conductor the current is proportional to the voltage and inversely proportional to the resistance.

graphs.title: The current rises in a straight line as the voltage rises.
graphs.label: Current

graphs.title: Drag the point along the graph to change the resistance and watch the current.
graphs.label: Current

sentences: Try a resistance of 4 ohm and then 20 ohm at the same voltage.

concept_check.question: If the voltage stays the same and the resistance is doubled, what happens to the current?
concept_check.explanation: The current is inversely proportional to the resistance, so doubling the resistance halves the current.

hints: Change one control at a time.
What happens to the current when the voltage rises and the resistance stays the same?
Current equals voltage divided by resistance.
